name: Multiply RHEL
description: Distributor-led demand generation campaign surfacing hidden RHEL opportunities through two-layer channel leverage.

narratives.name: Practice Intent
narratives.description: Why Multiply RHEL requires a structured distributor-led campaign approach and how this practice addresses the challenge.

narrativeContexts.context: Across MENA and adjacent regions, an estimated 10,000+ enterprise Linux workloads run unsupported CentOS, Oracle Linux, or community distributions without enterprise backing. These workloads represent latent RHEL subscription revenue invisible to Red Hat's direct sales organization, accessible only through distributor-reseller networks that hold existing customer relationships.

The Multiply RHEL campaign activates a two-layer channel cascade where one distributor recruits and enables 5+ resellers, each reaching 5+ end customers, producing 25x reach amplification. Resellers are equipped through half-day bootcamps with four RHEL sales play prototypes (Security, AI, Modernization, Extended Support), conversation starter kits, and TCO/ROI calculators that transform product-focused conversations into value-led customer engagements.

Pipeline attribution tracks campaign performance through leading indicators (partners activated, workshops delivered, deal registrations submitted) and lagging indicators ($3M deal registrations, $2M qualified pipeline, $1M closed revenue), with play-level and partner-level granularity enabling data-driven optimization.

Campaign performance analysis drives wave-two expansion, play refinement based on win/loss data, and channel mix optimization, establishing a repeatable distributor campaign model deployable across additional product lines and regions.

narratives.description: How RHEL campaign opportunities progress from identification through closure and expansion.

narrativeContexts.context: RHEL conversion opportunities emerge from the campaign's customer workshops and discovery sessions, where resellers identify enterprises running unsupported or competitive Linux with quantifiable migration potential ranging from $3K to $150K ARR per account.

Each qualified opportunity must progress through deal registration with campaign attribution, technical validation through POC with Red Hat SA support, and commercial closure through the authorized channel to capture the full incentive stack.

Resellers submit deal registrations with campaign codes, play designation, and RHEL tier identification. Red Hat SAs co-sell on qualified opportunities, delivering POCs that validate migration feasibility and business value. Weekly pipeline reviews maintain deal velocity through the campaign cycle.

Closed deals generate RHEL subscription revenue with full incentive realization, establish customer incumbency for renewal positioning, and create expansion pathways into Satellite, OpenShift, and RHEL AI that compound lifetime customer value beyond the initial conversion.

narratives.name: Execution Guidance
narratives.description: How to conduct customer discovery workshops for RHEL opportunity qualification.

narrativeContexts.context: Customer discovery workshops are the primary face-to-face touchpoint in the campaign cascade, identifying Linux workloads, validating RHEL fit, and qualifying conversion opportunities.

Follow a three-phase structure: (1) Environment discovery mapping the customer's Linux landscape (distributions, versions, workload count, support status), (2) Pain point validation confirming business drivers (security, compliance, cost, modernization), (3) RHEL value proposition presenting the relevant play prototype with TCO/ROI evidence. Qualify using the campaign framework: workloads to convert, buying authority, budget, timeline, technical feasibility. Document workshop outcomes in the post-workshop summary template.

Avoid leading with RHEL product features before establishing the customer's pain. The workshop should discover the customer's Linux landscape first, then match the appropriate play prototype to the confirmed business drivers.

narrativeContexts.context: The RHEL technical POC validates migration feasibility, operational improvement, and business value in the customer's own environment, co-delivered by Red Hat SA and partner.

Scope the POC based on the qualified play: Convert2RHEL migration assessment for Security play, RHEL AI workload deployment for AI play, OpenShift Virtualization demonstration for Modernization play, or lifecycle extension validation for Extended Support play. Demonstrate three things: technical feasibility, operational improvement (security posture, management overhead), and business value (TCO/ROI with real customer data). Document results in a customer-facing summary.
Avoid running generic RHEL demos disconnected from the customer's specific workloads and pain points. The POC must validate the specific migration or deployment pathway identified during discovery.

Analyze across three dimensions: Partners (activation rates, performance distribution), Customers (workshops, qualification rates, conversion), and Product Line (SKU mix, upsell rates). Calculate leading-to-lagging indicator correlation. Produce pipeline/revenue snapshot comparison (start date, current, end date plus 30 days). Generate optimization recommendations: shift channel investment, provide additional enablement to underperformers, double down on effective plays, capture wave-two nominations.

Avoid optimizing for activity volume (more workshops, more events) when conversion quality is the issue. Analyze the conversion funnel to identify where qualified leads stall rather than increasing top-of-funnel activity.

narrativeContexts.context: Market trigger identification systematically scans partner territories to surface the hidden RHEL opportunity landscape across customer bases running unsupported or competitive Linux.

Apply trigger framework across five categories: (1) CentOS/community Linux exposure with workloads running unsupported distributions, (2) Commercial Linux renewal pressure from Oracle, SUSE, or alternatives, (3) VMware exit and modernization initiatives, (4) AI infrastructure buildout requiring enterprise-grade OS, (5) Extended lifecycle needs for RHEL 6/7.
